title: Come On
cn: 第 22 集 · 来吧，下雨吧
novel:
The [[forecast|forecast]] promised a clear sky, which was exactly the problem.

Robin had plans to leave the city for the weekend. Ted, out of ideas, decided that only bad weather could keep her — so, at midnight, he stood on the roof and performed a [[chant|chant]] he had found online, half joke and half [[plea|plea]].

"Come on," he shouted at the stars.

Marshall thought it was a [[miracle|miracle]] when the first [[gust|gust]] of wind arrived. Then came the [[thunder|thunder]], then white [[lightning|lightning]], then a [[downpour|downpour]] so heavy that the street turned into one long [[puddle|puddle]].

Ted had no [[umbrella|umbrella]] and did not look for [[shelter|shelter]]. He walked twenty blocks and was completely [[drenched|drench]], [[soaked|soaked]] to the skin, feeling [[vulnerable|vulnerable]] and strangely calm.

At her [[doorstep|doorstep]] he found his [[courage|courage]]. No clever speech, no [[ultimatum|ultimatum]]; just the truth, said badly, in the rain.

It was a [[turning point|turning point]]. Whatever came next — [[heartbreak|heartbreak]] or happiness — he had finally stopped waiting for [[fate|fate]] to do the work for him.

In the [[aftermath|aftermath]], soaking wet and laughing, he understood that this night would be [[unforgettable|unforgettable]] — and that the story he would tell his children had only just begun.

forecast.en: a report that says what the weather will be

chant.en: words said again and again in a rhythm

miracle.en: a wonderful thing that seems impossible

thunder.en: the loud noise you hear in a storm

lightning.en: the bright flash of light in a storm

downpour.en: a lot of rain falling very fast

puddle.en: a small pool of rain water on the ground

umbrella.en: the thing you hold over your head in the rain

shelter.en: a place that keeps you safe from rain or danger

vulnerable.en: easy to hurt, in body or in feelings

doorstep.en: the step just outside someone's front door

courage.en: the strength to do something frightening

ultimatum.en: a final demand: do this, or something bad happens

turning point.en: the moment when things start to change

heartbreak.en: very deep sadness, usually about love

fate.en: the power that people believe decides what happens

aftermath.en: the time just after something big or bad happens

unforgettable.en: so special that you can never forget it
